consumer_seed: The Ofcom telecoms complaints report was published on 25 January 2024.
The report was last updated on 30 July 2026.
Ofcom receives complaints about landline, fixed broadband, pay-monthly mobile and pay-TV services.
Ofcom publishes provider complaint volumes quarterly relative to customer base size, expressed per 100,000 customers.
The current report covers January to March 2026.
Overall complaints decreased in Q1 2026 compared with Q4 2025.
Fixed-broadband and pay-monthly-mobile complaints decreased in Q1 2026.
Landline and pay-TV complaints stayed at the same level in Q1 2026.
TalkTalk was the most complained-about fixed-broadband provider in Q1 2026.
Plusnet and Sky generated the fewest fixed-broadband complaints in Q1 2026.
Plusnet and TalkTalk generated the most landline complaints in Q1 2026.
EE, Sky, Utility Warehouse, Virgin Media and Vodafone were the least complained-about landline providers in Q1 2026.
Sky Mobile was the most complained-about pay-monthly-mobile provider in Q1 2026.
EE, Giffgaff, Tesco Mobile, Three and Vodafone generated the fewest pay-monthly-mobile complaints in Q1 2026.
EE and Virgin Media were the most complained-about pay-TV providers in Q1 2026.
The Ofcom ADR schemes performance page was published on 26 January 2024.
The ADR performance page was last updated on 23 July 2026.
Ofcom reports KPIs for CISAS and Communications Ombudsman.
Ofcom publishes both schemes' KPI results quarterly.
The displayed revised ADR KPIs apply from Q4 2025.
Communications Ombudsman answered 95% of calls within two minutes in Q2 2026.
Communications Ombudsman answered 98% of calls within five minutes in Q2 2026.
Communications Ombudsman replied to 97% of digital correspondence within three working days in Q2 2026.
Communications Ombudsman replied to 100% of written correspondence within 10 working days in Q2 2026.
Communications Ombudsman reached 99% of case decisions within six weeks in Q2 2026.
Communications Ombudsman issued less than 1% of case decisions later than eight weeks in Q2 2026.
CISAS answered 99% of calls within two minutes in Q2 2026.
CISAS answered 100% of calls within five minutes in Q2 2026.
CISAS replied to 96% of digital correspondence within three working days in Q2 2026.
CISAS replied to 100% of written correspondence within 10 working days in Q2 2026.
The Ofcom mobile-switching guide was published on 1 October 2016.
The mobile-switching guide was last updated on 1 July 2026.
A customer can text INFO to 85075 to check contract status.
A customer who wants to keep the number can text PAC to 65075.
A customer who wants a new number can text STAC to 75075.
A provider must return a PAC or STAC within one minute and the code is valid for 30 days.
After receiving the PAC or STAC, the new provider must complete the switch within one working day.
The Ofcom broadband-switching guide was published on 4 August 2010.
The broadband-switching guide was last updated on 1 July 2026.
Under One Touch Switch, the customer contacts the new provider and the new provider arranges the broadband switch.
A customer switching before the contract ends may face early termination charges and One Touch Switch provides information about charges.
The Ofcom contract checklist was published on 22 January 2014.
The contract checklist was last updated on 26 June 2026.
Providers must offer an option no longer than 12 months for each service, and residential or small-business service contracts should not exceed 24 months.
Before consent, customers should receive a written one-page contract summary, or three pages for bundled services, plus detailed written contract information before being bound.
expansion_rule: For each July 2026 BDUK contract emit fifteen records: supplier, contracted, built, contracted-minus-built gap, built share, share of displayed contracted total, share of displayed built total, contracted rank, built rank, gap rank, built-share rank, supplier contract count, supplier contracted total, supplier built total and supplier built share. Append 45 Ofcom complaint, ADR, mobile switching, broadband switching and contract-checklist records. Equal numeric values share competition rank. Every fifth expanded record is REVALIDATION; all others are UPGRADE.
